problem_type: Unconsumed component bindings accumulate lint debt during UI ownership changes
symptom: Fresh lint over 521 TSX files reports 14 no-unused-vars warnings in six canvas/card/whiteboard consumers.
direct_cause: Unused imports and pure constants survive rendering changes; one hook result and three public props are still destructured without consumers.
class_root: A consumer binding must represent a real use without confusing removal of a binding with removal of its hook call, effect, public type, or operation.
affected_population: Canvas Base/preview and Character/Scene/Prop card renders
Whiteboard canvas progress props and existing operation callbacks
internal_only_reason: The invariant is determined by actual repository consumers, existing hook effects, public Props types and the unchanged ESLint configuration; no dependency or third-party runtime behavior is changed.
invariants: Keep JSX, class/style, visible text, conditions, callback arguments, and controls identical
Retain every hook call in its original relative position; discard only the unused result binding
Retain public Props fields, optionality, types and caller attributes; remove only unused parameter destructuring
Remove only imports and initializers proved unconsumed and pure
Do not alter Fast Refresh ownership, crowd memo dependencies, rules, warning limit, baseline, model/task routing, providers, i18n or stored data

door_reduction.why_not: All existing measurement and preview/whiteboard consumers must remain callable with the same Props and lifecycle. Removing dead local bindings does not justify merging components, removing observers/subscriptions, or changing public entry points.

generality_proof: A fresh TSX-only lint scan finds the complete no-unused population in six consumers. The unchanged lint owner catches unused imports/locals while focused AST tests retain the hook position, card measurement/upload/title consumers, public Props, and whiteboard callbacks. A before/after AST comparison additionally verifies unchanged JSX, public types, hook sequence and every other call.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Bind only consumed values, retaining the media measurement hook as an unconditional same-position call
Keep the public preview contract and operations while omitting unused local parameter bindings
Keep progress in public Props and preserve all whiteboard actions/hooks while omitting its unused local binding
Unchanged existing owner of measurements, ResizeObserver subscription and cleanup; never removed to satisfy lint

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Unused hook result becomes a standalone call; original neighbors and all hook expressions are retained
shotIndex/displayPrompt remain in public Props and caller attributes but no longer create unused local bindings
removingBackgroundProgress remains optional number|null in the public type; all operations stay bound
Independent measured-node consumer is not changed; no unused result is reported by fresh lint

recurrence.reason: Any later component extraction or rendering-owner move can leave unused imports, locals or parameter bindings with live hook effects behind them.
same_class_scan: Fresh pnpm exec eslint src/**/*.tsx: 521 files, 14 unused warnings in exactly six consumers
Actual imports/initializers, media measurement observer/cleanup, public Props and all local references read
Generated door map of useNodeMediaMeasurement, GenerationNodePreviewBody and LeaferCanvas: nine retained entries, including the existing preview Props type-read edge
Fast Refresh, exhaustive-deps/crowd memo and explicit-any warnings deliberately excluded from this approved batch

prevention.invariant: An unused result binding can disappear only while preserving the hook call and the existing public/rendering contract.
prevention.failure_mode: Unchanged no-unused-vars identifies residual unused values; focused AST regressions fail if the hook, Props, operations or card consumers disappear.
prevention.strategy: Clean the binding at each existing consumer rather than changing shared hooks, public contracts, styles or lint policy; retain the existing shared measurement owner.

legacy_paths.rationale: No callable legacy path or API is removed or replaced; only non-consumed local bindings, unused imports and pure constants disappear.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency controls this local binding invariant and no dependency/API/version is changed; existing React, DOM, TypeScript and ESLint owners remain in place.

migration: No data or caller migration. Existing Props fields and JSX callers stay intact; coordinator integrates only this small commit over its own handler/i18n changes.
residual_risks: The main total warning budget must be checked after integration; this isolated branch has different already-completed non-TSX batches
No real App/Provider/media acceptance is performed or claimed for this behavior-preserving static cleanup
Other Fast Refresh, memo dependency and any warnings remain intentionally outside this batch
